items.title: Leviathan mY: The Frame-by-Frame Analyst Who Made Chinese Animation Worth Watching Twice
items.summary: Leviathan mY is a Chinese animation and gaming analyst and one of the most distinctive figures in Bilibili's animation section. His account, which he has operated under the handle Leviathan mY since beginning uploads in the late 2010s, has accumulated approximately 1.94 million followers as…
items.content_html:
Leviathan mY is a Chinese animation and gaming analyst and one of the most distinctive figures in Bilibili's animation section. His account, which he has operated under the handle Leviathan mY since beginning uploads in the late 2010s, has accumulated approximately 1.94 million followers as of early 2026, and he has been named to Bilibili's annual Top 100 UP Creator list twice, for 2024 and 2025. His account registration date is August 1, though he has never publicly disclosed his real name or educational background. What distinguishes him from the vast majority of animation commentators on Chinese video platforms is his method: he approaches animated series and video games not as entertainment products to be consumed and reviewed but as dense visual texts to be read frame by frame, with every camera movement, color choice, and background detail treated as potential evidence for interpretive claims about the work's deeper meaning. His videos routinely run thirty minutes to an hour, and the production cycle for a single episode can extend beyond three weeks, a pace that places him among the most labor-intensive creators in Bilibili's animation ecosystem.

Leviathan mY began his Bilibili career in the late 2010s as a commentator on domestic animation, or guochuang, a category that Bilibili was actively promoting as part of its broader strategy to support Chinese-origin creative content. His early videos focused on series such as *The Legend of Qin* and *Mortals' Journey to Immortality*, and he quickly established a reputation for noticing details that other commentators overlooked. His analysis of *Mortals' Journey to Immortality*, for example, examined the internal logic of magical combat systems by tracing the consistency of rules across episodes, demonstrating that the series' apparent complexity was grounded in a coherent set of principles that the animation team had carefully maintained. This approach, which treats animation as a system of meaning rather than a sequence of spectacles, attracted an audience of viewers who wanted more from animation commentary than plot summary or emotional reaction. By 2021, he had accumulated approximately 500,000 followers and was selected for Bilibili's Top 100 UP Creator list for the first time. His growth continued steadily over the following years, and by January 2025 his follower count had reached approximately 1.526 million, rising to 1.937 million by early 2026.

What makes Leviathan mY's content structurally distinctive is the extreme granularity of his analysis and the sheer volume of research that supports it. His most celebrated project is a four-hundred-thousand-character analysis of *The Wandering Earth II*, the 2023 science fiction film directed by Frant Gwo. The video, which runs well over an hour, reconstructs the film's hidden narrative lines by cross-referencing visual details across the entire runtime, from the design of control panels to the positioning of background characters. It was not merely a review but a reconstruction of the film's implied world, and it became one of the most widely cited analyses of the film in Chinese-language media. His sixteen-part deep analysis of *Black Myth: Wukong*, the 2024 action role-playing game developed by Game Science, represents an even more ambitious undertaking. Across sixteen episodes released over several months, he examined the game's narrative structure, mythological references, environmental storytelling, and combat design, culminating in an interpretation of the game's ending that differed substantially from the readings offered by most other commentators. The series was widely praised for identifying details that even dedicated players had missed, and it established Leviathan mY as one of the most authoritative voices on the game's narrative complexity.

His other major works include comprehensive analyses of *The Legend of Qin*, one of China's longest-running animated series, and *Link Click*, a time-travel thriller that became one of the most critically acclaimed Chinese animations of the early 2020s. His analysis of *Link Click* focused on the series' use of visual clues to foreshadow plot developments, and he demonstrated that seemingly incidental details in early episodes functioned as deliberate setups for revelations in later seasons. This method of analysis, which he has described as treating the animation team as collaborators in a puzzle that the audience is invited to solve, has influenced a generation of younger animation commentators on Bilibili. His video on the animated series *The Ravages of Time*, adapted from the historical manga by Chan Mou, examined the series' treatment of political strategy and its fidelity to the source material, and it was cited by fans as an example of how adaptation analysis can illuminate both the original work and its animated interpretation.

The platform achievements of Leviathan mY reflect the growing institutional recognition of deep analysis as a legitimate and valuable form of animation content. His two consecutive Top 100 UP Creator selections, in 2024 and 2025, placed him alongside creators with audiences several times larger than his own, a recognition that reflects Bilibili's stated commitment to rewarding depth over mere popularity. His average video performance is substantial: his most successful analyses have accumulated millions of views, and his sixteen-part *Black Myth* series generated sustained engagement across its entire release period. In 2025, he was featured in media coverage of the Top 100 list as a representative of the animation analysis category, with journalists noting that his inclusion signaled the platform's recognition of "frame-by-frame interpretation" as a distinct and valued genre. He has also collaborated with animation studios and game developers, including a 2025 collaboration with the studio behind *Mortals' Journey to Immortality* for an exclusive interview with the series' director, demonstrating that his analytical work has earned the respect of the creators whose work he examines.

The broader social value of Leviathan mY's work lies in his demonstration that animation and video games are worthy of the same kind of close reading that literary scholars apply to novels and poems. In a media environment where animation is often dismissed as children's entertainment or treated as a niche passion with limited intellectual depth, his videos argue implicitly for the artistic seriousness of the medium. He does not approach animation with the assumption that it needs to be defended; he approaches it with the assumption that it contains layers of meaning that reward sustained attention. For viewers who have grown up with animation and who sense that there is more to their favorite series than they have consciously noticed, his videos offer a second experience of the work, one in which passive enjoyment is transformed into active interpretation. His emphasis on evidence and reasoning, rather than emotional declaration, models a way of engaging with popular culture that is both rigorous and passionate.

In summary, Leviathan mY represents a model of the creator as a visual close reader, someone who has built a significant audience by doing one thing exceptionally well rather than by chasing the latest trends. His nearly two million followers, his two Top 100 UP Creator selections, and his sixteen-part *Black Myth* analysis are all evidence that his method has resonated with viewers who want more from animation commentary than a recap of plot points. For Bilibili, he is a cornerstone of the animation section and a demonstration that the platform's community culture can sustain creators who prioritize depth over speed. For viewers, he offers a reminder that the most rewarding way to experience a great animated work is to watch it twice: once to enjoy it, and once to understand how it was made. His long-term significance lies in his demonstration that the most valuable cultural criticism is not the loudest but the most careful, and that an audience exists for content that respects their intelligence and invites them to see what they have been looking at all along.

items.title: Jueming Mofei: The Obsessive Analyst Who Turned Crime Drama into a Masterclass in Storytelling
items.summary: Jueming Mofei is a Chinese film and television commentator and one of the most respected voices in Bilibili's film section. His name is a deliberate cultural hybrid, combining a reference to the American television series *Breaking Bad* (known in Chinese as *Jueming Dushi*) with Murphy's…
items.content_html:
Jueming Mofei is a Chinese film and television commentator and one of the most respected voices in Bilibili's film section. His name is a deliberate cultural hybrid, combining a reference to the American television series *Breaking Bad* (known in Chinese as *Jueming Dushi*) with Murphy's Law, the adage that anything that can go wrong will go wrong. The name also evokes the character Murphy from Christopher Nolan's *Interstellar*, a figure who represents infinite possibility. This layered self-naming captures the intellectual sensibility he brings to his work: a fascination with the darker corners of human behavior, an appreciation for narrative structure and consequence, and a conviction that even the most disturbing stories can illuminate something essential about the world. As of early 2026, his Bilibili channel has over 1.88 million followers, and in January of that year he was named to the platform's annual Top 100 UP Creator list for 2025, a recognition that placed him among the most influential film commentators on the platform.

Jueming Mofei's path to becoming one of Bilibili's most rigorous film analysts was not built on formal training in film studies or media production. He has never claimed academic credentials in the field, and his public persona is defined less by biography than by method. His account is dedicated almost entirely to a single, demanding creative project: the deep, long-form analysis of crime, thriller, and suspense television series. He describes his approach as one of "obsessive" attention to detail, and the description is not hyperbole. Each video typically runs well over twenty minutes, and the most ambitious projects span dozens of episodes, each one dedicated to a single installment of a television series. He examines camera angles, lighting choices, musical cues, dialogue rhythm, and narrative structure with the precision of a scholar working through a primary text. He traces recurring motifs across seasons, identifies visual callbacks that casual viewers would never notice, and argues for interpretive readings that are grounded in evidence from the work itself rather than in abstract theory. His commentary is characterized by a tone that shifts fluidly between seriousness and humor, allowing him to address disturbing subject matter without becoming either exploitative or sanctimonious.

The scale of Jueming Mofei's output is itself a distinguishing feature of his channel. His most celebrated project is a complete, episode-by-episode analysis of *Breaking Bad*, a series that ran for sixty-two episodes across five seasons. He has produced a comparable complete breakdown of *Better Call Saul*, the prequel series that many critics consider equal or superior to its predecessor. His analysis of *Fargo*, the anthology crime drama, covers every season with the same exhaustive attention. He has also produced long-form series on *Narcos*, *The Godfather*, and a collection he calls the "Border Trilogy," focusing on crime stories set along international frontiers. His "Century of Crime Classics" collection, which gathers his analyses of canonical crime narratives, has accumulated nearly thirty million views. The consistency of this output over years of work reflects a creative discipline that is rare in the volatile ecosystem of online content, where creators often abandon long-term projects in favor of shorter, more algorithmically friendly formats.

What makes Jueming Mofei's analysis compelling to such a large audience is not merely the volume of detail he provides but the interpretive framework he applies to that detail. He approaches each series not as a puzzle to be solved but as a moral and psychological inquiry. His analysis of *Breaking Bad*, for example, is not primarily concerned with cataloging Walter White's crimes or charting his transformation from chemistry teacher to drug lord. It is concerned with the question of how a person justifies his own moral degradation to himself, and with the narrative techniques that the show's creators use to implicate the audience in that justification. His commentary on *Better Call Saul* explores the tragedy of a man whose gifts for manipulation become his prison, and he argues that the series is ultimately a study of how institutions shape individual destiny. These are not the conclusions of a reviewer summarizing plot points; they are the conclusions of a critic engaging seriously with the artistic choices that give a story its meaning. His willingness to disagree with popular interpretations, to revise his own earlier readings when new evidence emerges, and to acknowledge the ambiguity that great drama preserves rather than resolves has earned him a reputation for intellectual honesty that his audience values as much as his encyclopedic knowledge of the shows he covers.

Jueming Mofei's platform achievements, while modest in raw follower numbers compared to Bilibili's most popular entertainment creators, are significant in the context of film commentary. His 1.88 million followers represent a highly engaged audience that returns for long-form content requiring sustained attention. His selection to the 2025 Top 100 UP Creator list, announced in January 2026, placed him alongside creators with audiences several times larger than his own, a recognition that reflects the platform's stated commitment to rewarding depth over mere popularity. His "Century of Crime Classics" collection has accumulated nearly thirty million views across its constituent videos, demonstrating that his audience is willing to invest substantial time in rigorous analysis. His channel has become a reference point for Chinese viewers seeking to understand complex crime dramas, and his interpretations are frequently cited in discussions on other platforms. His approach has also influenced a generation of younger film commentators, many of whom have adopted the long-form, episode-by-episode format that he helped popularize in the Chinese-language context.

The broader social value of Jueming Mofei's work lies in his demonstration that popular entertainment can be treated with the same intellectual seriousness as literature or art. Crime dramas are often dismissed as genre entertainment, unworthy of the kind of close reading that scholars apply to canonical texts. Jueming Mofei's career is an argument against that dismissal. He shows that a television series can be constructed with the same attention to theme, structure, and visual language as a novel or a film, and that analyzing those elements is not an exercise in pretension but a way of deepening one's experience of the work. For viewers who come to his channel after finishing a series and wondering what they missed, his videos offer a second education, one that transforms passive consumption into active engagement. His emphasis on the moral and psychological dimensions of crime narratives, rather than on the spectacle of violence, provides a counterweight to the sensationalism that characterizes much of the true-crime genre. He treats the stories he analyzes as case studies in human behavior, and he invites his audience to think about why people do terrible things, how systems fail, and what it means to live with the consequences of one's choices.

In summary, Jueming Mofei represents a model of the creator as a devoted close reader, someone who has built a significant audience by doing one thing exceptionally well rather than by chasing the latest trend. His name, which combines a reference to one of the greatest television dramas ever made with a nod to the inevitability of things going wrong, is a fitting label for a body of work that is fundamentally concerned with consequence, causality, and the slow unraveling of carefully constructed lives. His 1.88 million followers, his Top 100 UP Creator recognition, and his thirty-million-view crime classics collection are all evidence that this approach has resonated. For Bilibili, he is a cornerstone of the film section and a demonstration that the platform can support creators who prioritize depth over speed. For viewers, he offers a reminder that the most rewarding way to watch a great story is to watch it twice: once to experience it, and once to understand how it was made.

items.title: Turing's Cat: The AI Researcher Who Turned Complex Technology into Bilibili's Most Accessible Science
items.summary: Turing's Cat, known in Chinese as Tuling de Mao, is a Chinese artificial intelligence researcher, technology entrepreneur, and one of Bilibili's most respected science and technology content creators. The account was founded in 2019 by Wang Yiran, a researcher with an academic background spanning the…
items.content_html:
Turing's Cat, known in Chinese as Tuling de Mao, is a Chinese artificial intelligence researcher, technology entrepreneur, and one of Bilibili's most respected science and technology content creators. The account was founded in 2019 by Wang Yiran, a researcher with an academic background spanning the Chinese University of Hong Kong and professional experience as an engineer at Amazon. The name is a deliberate intellectual homage, combining the surname of Alan Turing, the father of theoretical computer science and artificial intelligence, with a reference to Schrödinger's cat, the famous thought experiment in quantum mechanics. This dual reference captures the essence of the channel's mission: to make the most complex and abstract technologies of the twenty-first century accessible, tangible, and relevant to ordinary people. As of January 2025, the Bilibili channel has 1.085 million followers, and Wang Yiran's total following across all platforms exceeds 2.1 million. He was named to Bilibili's annual Top 100 UP Creator list in 2024 and again in 2026 for the 2025 list, recognition that places him among the platform's most influential voices in science and technology communication. He is also the founder of Creaibo, an AI-powered content creation tool developed by his company, which has been presented at industry events in Shanghai's Yangpu District as an example of the city's digital economy innovation.

Wang Yiran's path to becoming one of China's leading AI communicators was not a straight line from academia to media. He began his research career at the Chinese University of Hong Kong, where he studied artificial intelligence and developed the technical foundation that would later inform his public communication. He then worked as an engineer at Amazon, gaining practical experience in the technology industry and observing firsthand how AI systems were being deployed at scale. In 2019, while still working in the technology sector, he began uploading AI-related content to Bilibili, initially as a side project. At that time, artificial intelligence was still a relatively remote concept for most Chinese internet users, associated with science fiction and academic research rather than everyday life. Wang Yiran recognized that the gap between what AI researchers understood and what the general public knew was vast, and that the rapid pace of technological change was making that gap increasingly consequential. His first videos were explanatory and accessible, designed to demystify AI concepts without sacrificing accuracy. Over the following years, as AI moved from a niche academic subject to a dominant force in global technology and economics, his channel grew alongside the public's appetite for understanding it.

What distinguishes Turing's Cat from other technology creators on Bilibili is the depth of technical expertise that Wang Yiran brings to his content and his willingness to engage with AI at the level of research and development rather than merely reviewing consumer products. His videos cover topics ranging from the architecture of large language models and the mechanics of transformer networks to the practical applications of AI in content creation, scientific research, and everyday productivity. He has produced detailed analyses of major AI releases from companies such as OpenAI, Google, and Chinese developers, evaluating their capabilities and limitations with the rigor of someone who understands the underlying technology rather than merely reporting on marketing claims. His video on the Chinese AI model DeepSeek, released in early 2025, examined the technical innovations that allowed the model to achieve competitive performance at a fraction of the training cost of comparable Western systems, and it became one of his most widely viewed works, accumulating millions of views and generating extensive discussion across Chinese social media. The video's success reflected a broader moment in which Chinese audiences were hungry for informed, non-sensational analysis of their country's position in the global AI race.

Among his most significant contributions is the "AI Detailed Explanation" series, which functions as a structured curriculum for viewers who want to understand artificial intelligence from first principles. The series begins with the mathematical foundations of machine learning, moves through the history of neural network research, and culminates in detailed examinations of contemporary systems such as GPT, BERT, and diffusion models. Wang Yiran's teaching style is patient and methodical, and he frequently uses analogies and visual aids to make abstract concepts concrete. He does not assume prior technical knowledge, but he also does not simplify to the point of inaccuracy. This balance has made his content valuable to a wide range of viewers, from university students studying computer science to professionals in other fields who need to understand AI for their work. His videos on AI-generated content, including images, video, and music, have been particularly influential, providing both technical explanations and critical perspectives on the ethical and social implications of these technologies.

Turing's Cat's platform achievements reflect both his technical authority and his communication skill. His selection to Bilibili's Top 100 UP Creator list in 2024 and 2025 places him among a select group of technology creators recognized for sustained excellence. His follower count of over one million on Bilibili, while smaller than that of some entertainment creators, represents a highly engaged and technically literate audience that includes researchers, developers, entrepreneurs, and students. His company, Creaibo, has developed an AI creation tool that has been showcased at industry events and positioned as a practical application of the technologies he explains in his videos. In 2025, he participated in the Yangpu V-Park initiative, a Shanghai government-supported program designed to foster digital economy innovation, where he presented his team's work on AI-assisted content creation. His influence extends beyond Bilibili: his analyses are cited in Chinese technology media, and his videos are frequently referenced in discussions of AI policy, education, and industry development.

The broader social value of Wang Yiran's work lies in his role as a bridge between the frontier of AI research and the general public. In a period of rapid technological change, when AI systems are transforming industries, reshaping labor markets, and raising profound questions about creativity, privacy, and human agency, the ability of ordinary people to understand these technologies is not merely a matter of intellectual curiosity but of informed citizenship. Wang Yiran has built his audience by treating his viewers as capable of engaging with complex ideas, and his success demonstrates that there is a substantial demand for serious, accurate, and accessible AI education in China. His work has particular significance for young people considering careers in technology, who can use his videos as a supplement to formal education and as a guide to the skills and knowledge that will be most valuable in an AI-driven economy. At the same time, he has not shied away from addressing the risks and uncertainties associated with AI, including questions of misinformation, job displacement, and the concentration of technological power. His willingness to engage with these issues without resorting to either techno-utopianism or alarmism reflects an intellectual integrity that distinguishes his work from much of the hype-driven commentary that surrounds AI.

In summary, Turing's Cat represents a model of the creator as a public technologist, someone who has used the skills and knowledge acquired through academic research and industry experience to help a mass audience navigate the most consequential technological shift of the present era. Wang Yiran's journey from an AI researcher at the Chinese University of Hong Kong and Amazon to a leading voice in Chinese science communication reflects a deliberate choice to prioritize public understanding over purely academic or commercial pursuits. His one million followers on Bilibili, his two Top 100 UP Creator selections, and his recognition by Shanghai's digital economy initiatives are all evidence that this choice has been both intellectually and professionally successful. For Bilibili, he is a cornerstone of the platform's technology section and a demonstration that knowledge content can achieve both popularity and rigor. For viewers, he offers a reminder that the most important technologies are not those we use without thinking but those we take the time to understand. And for the broader landscape of Chinese digital culture, his career is a testament to the possibility of building a meaningful and influential public role by doing the hard work of explaining difficult things clearly.

items.title: Liangfeng Kaze: The "Countless Reviews" Creator Who Turned Anime Deduction into a Bilibili Institution
items.summary: Liangfeng Kaze, whose real name is Chen Yujia, is a Chinese anime and gaming content creator and one of the most recognizable figures in Bilibili's animation section. Born on November 18, 1991, in Shanghai, he graduated from Jinan University before beginning his video creation career…
items.content_html:
Liangfeng Kaze, whose real name is Chen Yujia, is a Chinese anime and gaming content creator and one of the most recognizable figures in Bilibili's animation section. Born on November 18, 1991, in Shanghai, he graduated from Jinan University before beginning his video creation career in January 2016 with an AMV (anime music video) titled "Only to Realize I Liked You, But It Was Already Too Late." Over the following decade, he transformed from a niche AMV editor into one of the platform's most durable and influential creators, known primarily for his "Countless Reviews" (阅片无数) series, which has become a defining format in Chinese anime commentary. As of early 2026, his Bilibili channel has over 7 million followers, and his videos have accumulated hundreds of millions of views across more than 1,500 uploads. He has been named to Bilibili's annual Top 100 UP Creator list three times, in 2019, 2020, and 2022, and he received the platform's Danmaku Popularity Award in 2020, a recognition tied specifically to the interactive comment culture that defines Bilibili's community.

Liangfeng Kaze's path to becoming one of Bilibili's most respected animation creators was gradual rather than meteoric. His early work consisted primarily of AMV edits, a genre in which creators synchronize anime footage with music to create emotional or dramatic montages. These videos, released under the series title "Liangfeng's Comedy Theater" (凉风滑稽小剧场), established his reputation for sharp editing instincts and a distinctive sense of humor. But it was the launch of the "Countless Reviews" series in 2019 that transformed his career. The format was deceptively simple: viewers would send him descriptions, screenshots, or fragments of anime they could not identify, and he would use his encyclopedic knowledge of the medium to track down the source. A viewer might remember only a single frame, a character's hairstyle, or a half-forgotten plot point; Liangfeng Kaze would reconstruct the full context from these fragments, often identifying obscure OVAs, vintage series, and forgotten films that had been out of circulation for decades. The series exploded in popularity, driving his follower count from approximately 2 million to over 5 million within a single year, and it remains the cornerstone of his channel to this day.

What distinguishes Liangfeng Kaze's content from other anime commentary on Bilibili is the combination of forensic deduction and genuine emotional investment that he brings to every episode. The "Countless Reviews" format is not merely a trivia game; it is an exercise in collective memory and cultural preservation. Many of the series he identifies are works that have never been officially released in China, that exist only in low-quality fan subtitles, or that have been effectively forgotten by the mainstream anime community. By tracking them down and presenting them to his audience, he functions as a kind of archivist of anime's overlooked corners. His commentary is characterized by a warm, conversational delivery that avoids both academic detachment and fanatical enthusiasm. He treats his viewers as collaborators in a shared project of discovery, and the interactive nature of the format—viewers submit queries, he responds with solutions—creates a sense of community that is rare in a creator-audience relationship. His other series, including "What's Up with New Anime" (新番咋了), "What's Up with Chinese Animation" (国创咋了), and "Fan Q&A" (粉丝问答), extend this collaborative spirit into seasonal reviews, industry analysis, and direct engagement with his audience.

Among his most representative works are episodes of "Countless Reviews" that have accumulated over 13 million views, including "My Wife Is Still in the Gacha Pool" and "The Girl Confessed on the Spot to Stop a Guy from Jumping." These titles, which blend anime fandom terminology with everyday scenarios, exemplify his ability to make the search for an obscure anime feel like a shared adventure rather than a solitary research task. His 2020 video "I Went to 'Join the Army'" documented his participation in a national defense education program organized by the Shanghai Garrison Command and Bilibili, in which he experienced military life and shared it with his audience. The video accumulated over 8 million views and demonstrated his willingness to step outside the anime niche into broader cultural and civic engagement. His 2025 collaboration with the Dejiang Nuo Opera cultural preservation project in Guizhou Province further extended his reach, as he produced a documentary about the endangered ritual theater tradition for an audience that had never encountered it before.

Liangfeng Kaze's platform achievements reflect both his sustained popularity and his institutional recognition. His three Top 100 UP Creator selections—2019, 2020, and 2022—place him among a select group of animation creators who have achieved repeated recognition over multiple years. His 2020 Danmaku Popularity Award acknowledged his unique relationship with Bilibili's comment culture; his videos generate tens of thousands of danmaku messages per episode, as viewers collectively participate in the identification process alongside him. His follower count has fluctuated over the years, reaching a peak of approximately 7.6 million before settling at around 7 million as of early 2026, a figure that still places him among the platform's most-followed animation creators. His commercial collaborations include partnerships with major game companies and brands targeting the anime demographic, and his live streaming activities have built a separate audience of viewers who value his real-time commentary and interaction.

The broader social significance of Liangfeng Kaze's career lies in his demonstration that niche expertise can be a foundation for mainstream success. Anime is often treated as a subculture with limited appeal beyond its dedicated fanbase, but Liangfeng Kaze's ability to attract millions of viewers to videos about obscure OVA identification suggests that the desire for connection, discovery, and shared memory transcends any particular content niche. His work has also contributed to the preservation of anime history in China, creating a searchable, accessible archive of series that might otherwise have been lost to obscurity. At the same time, his career has not been without controversy. In April 2021, he uploaded a video that functioned as a tutorial in "doxxing"—using publicly available information to identify the location where a photograph was taken, at the request of a viewer who claimed to be helping a friend. The video, which accumulated over a million views before being deleted, drew widespread criticism from media outlets and viewers who argued that it demonstrated techniques that could be used for harassment or privacy violations. Liangfeng Kaze issued a public apology, stating that he would not re-upload the video and would keep it as a personal reminder of his error. The incident, while serious, did not derail his career, and his subsequent work has been characterized by a greater sensitivity to the ethical implications of his content.

In summary, Liangfeng Kaze represents a model of the creator as a communal archivist and detective, someone who has built a mass audience by treating the identification of obscure anime as a collective project rather than a solitary pursuit. His "Countless Reviews" series is not merely entertainment; it is a living archive of a medium's forgotten history, maintained by a creator who takes his audience's memories seriously. His three Top 100 UP Creator selections, his Danmaku Popularity Award, and his seven million followers are all evidence of the trust he has earned over a decade of consistent, thoughtful work. For Bilibili, he is a cornerstone of the animation section and a demonstration that the platform's community culture—built around danmaku, collaboration, and shared expertise—can sustain creators whose appeal is rooted in genuine knowledge rather than algorithmic optimization. For viewers, he offers a reminder that the most rewarding content is often that which helps us find what we had forgotten we were looking for.

items.title: Lugdunum's Augustine: The Medievalist Who Made the Dark Ages a Bilibili Sensation
items.summary: Lugdunum's Augustine, known simply as Augustine to his followers, is a Chinese history content creator and one of the most distinctive figures in Bilibili's knowledge section. His channel name is a layered reference: Lugdunum is the ancient Roman name for Lyon, the French city where…
items.content_html:
Lugdunum's Augustine, known simply as Augustine to his followers, is a Chinese history content creator and one of the most distinctive figures in Bilibili's knowledge section. His channel name is a layered reference: Lugdunum is the ancient Roman name for Lyon, the French city where he pursued his doctoral studies, and Augustine evokes both the Christian theologian Saint Augustine of Hippo and the intellectual tradition of medieval scholasticism. He is a native of Jinan, Shandong Province, born in the mid-1990s, and he holds a doctorate in medieval European history and church history from a French university. He describes himself with characteristic self-deprecation as "an old man telling stories under the banyan tree at the village entrance," a phrase that captures the disarmingly casual tone he brings to subjects that most Chinese audiences would consider forbiddingly obscure. His Bilibili channel has accumulated over one million followers, and in January 2026 he was named to the platform's annual Top 100 UP Creator list for 2025, a recognition that placed him alongside creators with audiences many times larger than his own.

Augustine's path to content creation was neither planned nor gradual. He began uploading videos to Bilibili in March 2022, while he was still living in France completing his doctoral research. In an interview with The Paper, he explained that he was encouraged by his family to try video creation, a suggestion he initially treated as a casual experiment rather than a career pivot. His first video, uploaded without professional equipment or a developed creative plan, accumulated over 2.6 million views, an extraordinary debut for a creator with no prior platform presence. The success was not the result of algorithmic luck or a viral gimmick. It was the consequence of a simple insight: Augustine possessed something that very few Chinese-language content creators had, which was genuine academic expertise in a subject that Chinese audiences had encountered only through Hollywood films, fantasy novels, and video games. Medieval Europe, with its cathedrals, crusades, feudal hierarchies, and papal politics, was a familiar imaginative landscape for Chinese viewers, but it was almost never explained by someone who had actually studied its primary sources, read its Latin and French documents, and understood its institutional complexities from the inside.

What distinguishes Augustine's content from the vast field of Chinese history communication is the combination of scholarly rigor and narrative accessibility that he brings to every subject. His videos are meticulously researched; he has stated that each video requires approximately two weeks of source analysis, scriptwriting, and editing, and that he consults primary documents in Latin and Old French alongside secondary scholarship in multiple languages. Yet the presentation is anything but academic. He speaks in a relaxed, conversational register, punctuating his explanations with humorous asides, rhetorical questions, and references to contemporary culture that make the material feel immediate rather than remote. His video titles often adopt a provocative or playful tone: "How Did the Pope Scheme and Survive in Medieval Europe?", "Was King Arthur a Real Person or a Literary Invention?", "Why Could Football Only Have Been Born in England?". These titles draw viewers in with the promise of a satisfying answer to a question they did not know they had, and the videos deliver on that promise by building arguments from evidence rather than simply recounting familiar legends. His video length averages around twenty-five minutes, and despite this duration, his content maintains unusually high completion rates, a metric that Bilibili founder Chen Rui cited in a 2026 speech as evidence that young users are willing to invest sustained attention in high-quality long-form knowledge content.

The core of Augustine's creative output is a series of interconnected video projects on medieval European history and the institutional development of the Catholic Church. The "Popes and Papal Power" series, which he has been releasing in installments since 2023, traces the evolution of the papacy from a marginal bishopric in Rome to the dominant political and spiritual authority of medieval Christendom. The series examines papal elections, the conflicts between popes and emperors, the Great Schism of 1054, and the institutional mechanisms through which the Church consolidated its power. A separate series on the Western Schism explores the period between 1378 and 1417 when rival claimants to the papacy divided Europe along political lines, a subject that Augustine treats not as an arcane ecclesiastical dispute but as a case study in how institutional legitimacy is contested and reconstructed. His videos on the Crusades examine the motivations of participants, the logistical realities of medieval warfare, and the long-term consequences of the encounters between Latin Christendom and the Islamic world. Beyond explicitly religious and political subjects, he has produced videos on the history of bread, the origins of aristocratic surnames, the development of medieval universities, and the cultural significance of courtly love. This range reflects his conviction that medieval history is not a narrow specialty but a lens through which to understand the foundations of modern European institutions, from legal systems and universities to the separation of church and state.

Augustine's platform achievements, while modest in absolute numbers compared to Bilibili's most popular entertainment creators, are significant in the context of knowledge content. His follower count surpassed one million in 2025, and his videos consistently generate hundreds of thousands of views, with his most popular works exceeding two million. In January 2026, he was named to Bilibili's 2025 Top 100 UP Creator list, a selection that was widely noted in media coverage as evidence of the platform's commitment to supporting niche intellectual content. The Paper described his inclusion as a signal that "young users' demand for deep knowledge and preference for high-quality long-form video" were reshaping the value system of Chinese content creation. His selection alongside creators like He Tongxue, Luo Xiang, and Fangstafu placed him in the company of Bilibili's most respected knowledge communicators, and his acceptance speech, in which he expressed surprise at the recognition, was received by his audience as characteristic of his unassuming public persona. In April 2026, Bilibili founder Chen Rui cited Augustine's channel in a keynote address at the China Network Audio-Visual Conference as an example of how the platform's community can support creators who begin with small audiences and grow through consistent, high-quality output.

The broader social value of Augustine's work lies in his demonstration that expertise is not a barrier to popularity but a foundation for it. He did not simplify medieval history into easily digestible anecdotes; he explained complex institutional dynamics with the same patience and precision he would bring to a scholarly lecture, and his audience followed him. For Chinese viewers who have encountered the Middle Ages primarily through fantasy fiction and historical dramas, his videos offer a corrective: a picture of the medieval world that is grounded in evidence, attentive to uncertainty, and honest about what historians do and do not know. His willingness to acknowledge the limits of the evidence, to present competing interpretations, and to explain why certain questions remain unresolved distinguishes his work from the confident pronouncements of popular history content. In a media environment where expertise is often dismissed as elitism and where confident assertion is frequently rewarded over careful reasoning, Augustine represents a counterexample: a scholar who has found a mass audience by doing what scholars are trained to do, which is to ask precise questions, evaluate evidence, and explain the reasoning behind every conclusion.

In summary, Lugdunum's Augustine represents a model of the creator as a public scholar, someone who has translated the skills and habits of academic research into a form that works on a video platform without sacrificing the intellectual standards of his discipline. His first video's remarkable success was not an anomaly but the beginning of a sustained project to bring medieval European history to an audience that had never been offered it in a serious form. His one million followers, his Top 100 UP Creator recognition, and his citation by Bilibili's founder as a model of quality content all reflect the judgment that his work has earned from both the platform and its users. For Bilibili, he is evidence that the knowledge section can support creators who take the long view, investing weeks in research for a single video rather than chasing the rapid turnover of trending topics. For viewers, he offers a reminder that the most rewarding educational experiences are often those that require patience and attention, and that a subject as distant and unfamiliar as medieval church history can become vividly alive in the hands of someone who genuinely understands it.

items.title: Mazu Bobiya: The International Affairs Storyteller Who Makes Geopolitics Feel Like a Conversation
items.summary: Mazu Bobiya is a Chinese international affairs content creator and one of the most recognizable voices in Bilibili's knowledge section. His channel, which operates under the name “Mazu Bobiya” (麻薯波比呀), has accumulated over 3.05 million followers on Bilibili as of early 2025, with his following…
items.content_html:
Mazu Bobiya is a Chinese international affairs content creator and one of the most recognizable voices in Bilibili's knowledge section. His channel, which operates under the name “Mazu Bobiya” (麻薯波比呀), has accumulated over 3.05 million followers on Bilibili as of early 2025, with his following continuing to grow to approximately 3.44 million by late 2025. He also maintains a significant presence on Douyin, Weibo, and Tencent News, where he is officially verified as an international affairs creator, and he hosts a podcast on Qingting FM titled “Mazu Bobiya Talks Current Affairs”. His channel's tagline, “Life is hard, have some mochi,” captures the tone that has made him distinctive in a field often characterized by either dry academic analysis or inflammatory commentary. He approaches international politics, economics, and social issues with a blend of humor, narrative craft, and genuine analytical depth, treating his viewers as intelligent participants in a conversation rather than passive recipients of conclusions. In 2024, he received Bilibili's “Golden Knowledge Award” (Jin Zhi Jiang), the platform's highest recognition for knowledge creators, and his work has been incorporated into university general education course materials, a rare distinction for an independent online commentator.

Mazu Bobiya's path to becoming one of Bilibili's most respected international affairs commentators was neither quick nor easy. In a reflective post on his Bilibili dynamic in April 2024, he acknowledged that the first two years of building his account were “quite a struggle.” He described a period when he could barely afford basic expenses, recalling days when he spent only twenty yuan on food. This period of financial precarity shaped his approach to content creation in ways that remain visible in his work. He did not have the resources to produce high-budget videos or to chase viral trends, so he focused on what he could control: the quality of his analysis, the clarity of his explanations, and the consistency of his output. His background is not one of elite academic credentials or institutional affiliation. He is a native of Zhuhai, Guangdong Province, and his public profiles describe him simply as an international affairs enthusiast who built his expertise through years of independent study and observation. This outsider status, rather than being a disadvantage, has allowed him to approach international politics without the disciplinary constraints that sometimes make academic commentary inaccessible to general audiences.

What distinguishes Mazu Bobiya from the crowded field of Chinese international affairs commentators is his commitment to what he describes as “fun narrative style” (quweihua xushi fengge) applied to serious subjects. He does not begin his videos with abstract theoretical frameworks or geopolitical doctrines. He begins with a story, a question, or a scenario that draws the viewer in before gradually introducing the analytical framework necessary to understand it. His videos on the United States' industrial policy, for example, do not open with a discussion of comparative advantage or trade theory. They open with the observation that despite years of government incentives and political rhetoric, American manufacturing has not returned to the levels promised by its architects, and they ask why. From that concrete puzzle, he builds an explanation that draws on economic history, institutional analysis, and comparative case studies. His delivery is conversational and often humorous, but the substance is rigorous. He cites data, references specific policies and their outcomes, and acknowledges uncertainty where it exists. He has been described as a creator who “explains international political economy and social issues with a fun narrative style,” a formulation that captures both the accessibility of his presentation and the seriousness of his analytical ambition.

Among his most representative works is the video “The Failure of American Industrial Reshoring: The Loss of State Capacity, How Much Longer Can America Hold On?”, which accumulated 3.08 million views and topped Bilibili's knowledge section weekly rankings upon its release. The video examined the structural obstacles to manufacturing repatriation in the United States, including labor market dynamics, supply chain dependencies, and the political economy of industrial policy. It was not a polemic; it was an analysis that took the stated goals of American policymakers seriously and then evaluated the evidence about whether those goals were being achieved. Other significant works include his coverage of the U.S. debt crisis, the German federal election, and the trajectory of European military autonomy. His year-end lectures, delivered in late 2024 and late 2025, became annual events for his audience, with the 2024 lecture, titled “One Step Forward! How Will China Greet 2025?”, being simulcast at multiple vocational colleges and accumulating 2.237 million views. These lectures function as comprehensive reviews of the year's major international developments, synthesizing months of individual videos into a coherent narrative about the trajectory of global politics.

Mazu Bobiya's platform achievements reflect both his audience reach and the institutional recognition he has earned. In 2024, he received Bilibili's Golden Knowledge Award, the platform's annual award for outstanding knowledge content, placing him alongside established figures in Chinese science communication and education. His videos have been used as teaching materials in university general education courses, and his cross-year lectures have been livestreamed to multiple educational institutions. His podcast, launched in December 2025, extended his reach into audio, allowing listeners to engage with his analysis during commutes and other activities where video viewing is impractical. His following on Weibo exceeds 445,000, and his Tencent News account is verified as an international affairs creator, indicating that his influence extends across the major Chinese content platforms. His average video performance reflects a dedicated audience: his content consistently generates hundreds of thousands of views, and his most successful videos reach the millions.

The broader social value of Mazu Bobiya's work lies in his demonstration that international affairs commentary can be both accessible and intellectually serious. In a media environment where geopolitical discussion is often polarized between nationalist celebration and alarmist pessimism, he maintains a tone of analytical curiosity that treats international politics as a domain of genuine complexity rather than a stage for predetermined conclusions. His willingness to acknowledge the struggles of his early career, including the period when he could barely afford to eat, gives his success narrative a relatability that more polished creators often lack. For young viewers who are interested in international affairs but find academic literature intimidating or mainstream commentary unsatisfying, he offers a model of engagement that is rigorous without being exclusive. His incorporation into university curricula suggests that his work is being recognized not merely as popular content but as a legitimate educational resource, a distinction that few online commentators achieve.

In summary, Mazu Bobiya represents a model of the creator as a public analyst of international affairs, someone who treats geopolitical questions as puzzles to be worked through rather than positions to be defended. He built his audience not through institutional backing or inherited authority but through years of consistent, careful work during a period of financial difficulty. His Golden Knowledge Award and his adoption into university teaching materials reflect the recognition that his approach has earned from both the platform and the educational establishment. For Bilibili, he is evidence that the platform's knowledge section can support creators who take international politics seriously without descending into sensationalism. For viewers, he offers a reminder that understanding the world requires patience, evidence, and a willingness to revise one's assumptions. His long-term significance lies in his demonstration that the most valuable commentary is not the loudest but the most carefully reasoned, and that an audience exists for content that respects their intelligence and invites them to think alongside the creator rather than simply agree with him.

items.title: China BOY: The "Great Ape" Who Turned Absurd Games into a Generation's Shared Language
items.summary: China BOY, whose real name is Wang Hanzhe, is a Chinese gaming commentator, live streamer, and one of the most enduring figures in Bilibili's game section. Born on June 2, 1998, in Guiyang, Guizhou Province, he is known across the platform by his full handle,…
items.content_html:
China BOY, whose real name is Wang Hanzhe, is a Chinese gaming commentator, live streamer, and one of the most enduring figures in Bilibili's game section. Born on June 2, 1998, in Guiyang, Guizhou Province, he is known across the platform by his full handle, China BOY Super Gorilla, a name that has become so synonymous with his persona that most viewers simply call him "China BOY" or "the Gorilla". His life story is one of unusual early independence and sustained self-direction. His mother passed away in December 2007, when he was nine years old, and he was subsequently raised by his grandmother. He began producing game commentary videos in 2012, at the age of fourteen, using little more than a mobile phone and a rudimentary understanding of video editing. After completing high school in 2016, he made the decision not to attend university, concluding that video creation offered a viable and meaningful career path. That same year, he moved alone from Guiyang to Shanghai to pursue content creation full-time, a decision that placed him among the earliest cohort of Chinese creators to treat online video as a profession rather than a hobby. As of late 2025, his Bilibili channel has over 10.5 million followers, and his total reach across Bilibili, Douyin, and other platforms exceeds twenty million.

China BOY's content is defined by a deliberate and consistent refusal to engage with the games that dominate mainstream gaming media. He rarely features competitive esports titles or AAA blockbusters. Instead, his videos are built around what Chinese internet culture calls "shadiao games," a term that translates roughly as absurdist, deliberately low-quality, or bizarrely conceived games that most creators would never consider covering. He has described himself as one of the people in China who has played the greatest number of these games, and the claim is credible. His library includes simulations of mundane occupations, horror games built almost entirely around jump scares, and independent titles that are technically crude but conceptually strange. His commentary transforms these games into comedic material through a combination of exaggerated reactions, absurdist commentary, and a voice that fans have described as one of the most distinctive in Chinese gaming content. The humor is not cruel; he treats even the worst games with a kind of affectionate curiosity, approaching them as artifacts of human creativity rather than as products to be evaluated. This stance distinguishes him from reviewers who approach games as consumers and from entertainers who treat bad games as targets for mockery. For China BOY, a strange game is an invitation to explore, and his willingness to take that invitation seriously is what makes his content compelling.

Among his most influential works is the "China BOY Commentary" series, which has been running in various forms since his earliest years on the platform. The series encompasses hundreds of videos across a wide range of games, and its longevity reflects the consistency of his creative voice. The 2013 series "Games Are Really Weird" established the template that he would refine over the following decade: a game that appears ordinary or poorly made is played with genuine curiosity, and the comedy emerges from the gap between the game's ambitions and its execution. The "Wang Xiansheng, Your Ghost Videos" series, in which he reacts to fan-made remixes and compilations of his own content, became one of his most popular recurring formats in the life section. His collaboration videos with other prominent Bilibili creators, particularly those in the loose collective sometimes referred to as the "Shanghai help group," including Lao Fanqie, Mou Huanjun, and Hu Shaobei, generated some of the platform's most-watched collaborative content. In 2022, he extended his creative reach into game development itself with the release of "A Piece of Poo" on Steam, a game in which players control a piece of excrement on a journey of self-improvement and combat, which accumulated hundreds of reviews and demonstrated his willingness to participate in the culture he had spent a decade commenting on.

China BOY's platform achievements are substantial and sustained. He has been selected for Bilibili's Top 100 UP Creator list in multiple years, including 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2023, a record of recognition that spans the platform's most formative period of growth. In 2018, he received Bilibili's Annual Danmaku Popularity Award, a recognition specifically tied to the interactive comment system that is central to the platform's culture. In 2019, he was named one of Tencent's Game Persons of the Year. His channel consistently ranks among the most-followed gaming accounts on Bilibili, and his average video performance reflects a loyal and engaged audience rather than a purely algorithmic one. Beyond Bilibili, he has maintained a significant presence on Douyin, where he is a signed game livestreamer, and he has been recognized as a contracted artist under Chao Dian Culture, one of the platform's major creator management agencies. In 2021, he participated in the "Long Scroll Treasure Hunt" project, a Bilibili initiative in which prominent creators introduced historical and cultural landmarks, and he served as the guardian of key revolutionary sites in the Yangtze River Delta region, including the First National Congress of the Communist Party of China Memorial.

The broader social significance of China BOY's career lies in his demonstration that sustained success in Chinese digital media does not require formal credentials, institutional backing, or conformity to the expectations of the gaming industry. He left school at eighteen and built a career through a combination of creative instinct, relentless output, and an intuitive understanding of what his audience found funny. His decision to focus on games that no one else would cover created a niche that he has occupied almost entirely on his own for over a decade. For young viewers who see their own interests as marginal or unserious, his work offers validation: the strange, the absurd, and the deliberately low-quality can be treated with the same attention and care that mainstream culture reserves for prestige objects. His movement from game commentary into life vlogs, music, writing, and game development reflects a creative restlessness that has allowed him to remain relevant as platform trends have shifted. In 2026, he published a book titled "Let It Rain, Make a Friend," extending his presence into yet another medium, and his recognition as a "Z-generation China BOY" by state media for his ability to "tell China's story with sincerity" suggests that his cultural influence has been acknowledged beyond the platform's own ecosystem.

In summary, China BOY represents a model of the creator as an intuitive cultural archivist of the absurd. He has spent more than a decade documenting the strangest corners of the gaming world, and in doing so he has built one of the most durable and recognizable personas on Bilibili. His career began with a fourteen-year-old filming himself playing games on a phone; it has since encompassed live streaming, music, writing, game development, and collaborations with some of the platform's most prominent figures. He has been selected for the Top 100 UP Creator list four times, received the platform's danmaku popularity award, and maintained a following of over ten million people through periods of significant change in Bilibili's content ecosystem. For Bilibili, he is a foundational figure in the game section, someone who helped define what gaming commentary could be in the platform's early years and who has continued to evolve alongside it. For viewers, he is a reminder that the most enduring creative work is often the least prestigious, and that a genuine interest in the strange and overlooked can be a foundation for a career that lasts.

items.title: Fangstafu: The Paleontologist Couple Who Made Extinct Creatures Feel Alive
items.summary: Fangstafu is a Chinese science communication channel operated by Tang Cheng and his wife Cai Chunlin, dedicated to paleontology, evolutionary biology, and the broader life sciences. The channel's name is a phonetic transliteration of the English phrase "fun stuff," reflecting its founders' conviction that scientific…
items.content_html:
Fangstafu is a Chinese science communication channel operated by Tang Cheng and his wife Cai Chunlin, dedicated to paleontology, evolutionary biology, and the broader life sciences. The channel's name is a phonetic transliteration of the English phrase "fun stuff," reflecting its founders' conviction that scientific knowledge should be enjoyable, accessible, and emotionally resonant. Tang Cheng holds a doctorate from the Institute of Neuroscience at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, one of China's most prestigious research institutions, where his work focused on the neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior. Cai Chunlin, his wife and creative partner, manages the visual design, editing, and production aspects of the channel, creating the distinctive animated style that has become one of Fangstafu's most recognizable features. The couple began uploading videos to Bilibili in 2019, while Tang Cheng was still a doctoral student, and by 2020, after his graduation, they made the decision to pursue science communication as a full-time career rather than following the conventional academic path of postdoctoral research and university faculty positions. That decision, which Tang Cheng has described as a departure from what his academic training had prepared him for, has resulted in one of the most successful and critically respected science channels in China, with over 4.2 million followers on Bilibili as of early 2025 and a continuous presence on the platform's annual Top 100 UP Creator list since 2020.

The origin of Fangstafu's audience can be traced to a single video: "Anomalocaris: The Story of the First Hegemon," a thirty-minute animated documentary about a Cambrian-era predator that lived more than five hundred million years ago. The video, which combined rigorous paleontological research with a narrative structure that treated the ancient creature as a protagonist with a personality, ambitions, and a tragic destiny, accumulated millions of views and transformed the couple's hobby into a viable career. What made the video distinctive was not merely its subject matter, which had rarely been treated with such narrative seriousness in Chinese-language science communication, but its method. Tang Cheng approached the Anomalocaris not as a specimen to be described but as a character whose life could be reconstructed from fossil evidence. He explained the scientific debates surrounding the creature's anatomy, the competing hypotheses about its role in the Cambrian ecosystem, and the uncertainties that remain even after decades of research. The video did not simplify the science; it made the science feel urgent and dramatic by showing how paleontologists build knowledge from fragmentary evidence and how that knowledge changes as new fossils are discovered.

This commitment to narrative reconstruction has become Fangstafu's signature approach. The channel specializes in what its creators describe as "personified paleontology," a method in which extinct organisms are presented as characters whose behaviors, ecological roles, and evolutionary fates are explained through storytelling rather than through conventional lecture formats. The "Ghost Valley Chronicles" series, which focuses on the evolutionary history of vertebrates from fish to humans, represents the most ambitious expression of this approach. In one representative episode, the evolution of the mammalian ear is presented not as an anatomical transformation but as a story about the gradual repurposing of bones that once formed the jaw hinge of reptilian ancestors. The narrative follows the evidence: fossil intermediates, developmental biology, and comparative anatomy are woven together into a coherent account that respects scientific uncertainty while still providing a satisfying narrative arc. The series has been widely praised for its clarity and for its ability to make viewers feel that they are discovering the past alongside the researchers whose work is being described.

Beyond "Ghost Valley Chronicles," Fangstafu's content encompasses a wide range of topics within evolutionary biology and paleontology. The channel has produced episodes on the evolution of vision, the biology of parasites, the history of the domestication of plants and animals, and the ecological dynamics of mass extinction events. A recurring theme is the relationship between form and function: how the shape of a bone, the structure of an eye, or the arrangement of teeth can reveal what an organism ate, how it moved, and what pressures shaped its evolution. Tang Cheng's academic training in neuroscience informs his treatment of sensory biology, and several episodes have explored the evolution of the nervous system and the emergence of complex behavior. His wife Cai Chunlin's background in design and animation is evident in the visual style of the videos, which uses simple but expressive illustrations and animations to convey anatomical relationships and evolutionary sequences. The combination of scientific depth and visual clarity has made Fangstafu accessible to audiences ranging from university biology students to casual viewers with no formal scientific training.

The channel's institutional recognition has been substantial. Fangstafu received the Guokr Science Communication Contribution Award in 2020 and the Gezhi Science Communication Award as Creator of the Year in 2022. Tang Cheng was named one of Shanghai's "Science Stars" in 2025, a designation awarded by the municipal government to recognize outstanding contributions to public understanding of science. The channel has been selected for Bilibili's Top 100 UP Creator list in 2020, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025, a record of sustained recognition that places it among the platform's most consistently honored science accounts. In 2025, the "Ghost Valley Chronicles" series received the platform's Annual Original Program award, acknowledging the series' distinctive contribution to Bilibili's knowledge ecosystem. The couple has also collaborated with major brands and institutions, including a 2025 partnership with the mobile game Azur Lane for a public welfare initiative focused on mangrove conservation, which took them to Hainan Province to document wetland ecosystems.

The social value of Fangstafu's work lies in its demonstration that scientific rigor and popular accessibility are not competing objectives. Tang Cheng and Cai Chunlin have built a mass audience by treating their viewers as capable of understanding complex scientific ideas, provided those ideas are presented with sufficient clarity and narrative coherence. Their channel has filled a significant gap in Chinese-language science communication, which historically has been dominated by either technical academic content inaccessible to general audiences or superficial popularizations that sacrifice accuracy for entertainment. By occupying the space between these extremes, Fangstafu has helped establish a model for what serious science communication can look like on Chinese video platforms. For younger viewers, particularly those who may be considering careers in science, the channel offers a vision of scientific work as an ongoing process of discovery rather than a collection of settled facts. The couple's decision to leave conventional academic careers in order to pursue public communication full-time is itself a statement about the value they place on making science accessible, and their success suggests that this value is shared by millions of viewers.

In summary, Fangstafu represents a distinctive model of the creator as scientific storyteller. Tang Cheng and Cai Chunlin have combined advanced academic training with narrative skill and visual creativity to produce a body of work that is both scientifically rigorous and genuinely engaging. Their focus on paleontology and evolutionary biology, subjects that are often treated as remote and technical, has demonstrated that even the most ancient and unfamiliar forms of life can be made to feel immediate and meaningful when they are presented as characters in a story about survival, adaptation, and the long history of life on Earth. For Bilibili, Fangstafu is evidence that the platform's knowledge section can support creators who take intellectual risks and trust their audiences to follow. For the broader landscape of Chinese science communication, the channel is a reminder that the most effective educational content is often that which treats the audience not as passive recipients of information but as participants in the ongoing human project of understanding the natural world.

items.title: Siwei Shiyanshi: The Self-Taught Polymath Who Turns Cold Knowledge into a Weapon of Curiosity
items.summary: Siwei Shiyanshi, which translates as "Thinking Laboratory," is a Chinese knowledge creator and one of the most distinctive voices in Bilibili's science and history section. His real name is Zhao Jiaqi, and he is based in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province. Before becoming a full-time content creator,…
items.content_html:
Siwei Shiyanshi, which translates as "Thinking Laboratory," is a Chinese knowledge creator and one of the most distinctive voices in Bilibili's science and history section. His real name is Zhao Jiaqi, and he is based in Xi'an, Shaanxi Province. Before becoming a full-time content creator, he worked as an ordinary office employee, a fact that distinguishes him from the many Bilibili knowledge creators who hold advanced degrees from elite universities. His parents were both middle school teachers, and he describes himself as a student whose strengths lay in the sciences while his humanities performance was unremarkable. He has never claimed academic credentials he does not possess, and this honesty about his background has become part of his appeal. His channel's official description is disarmingly modest: "Science and historical knowledge popularization, with thinking added in. This is Thinking Laboratory, created entirely at home by one person. Starting a business is hard, so please be patient with updates". That single sentence captures the essence of his practice: a solo creator working from his apartment, producing videos that combine scientific rigor, historical analysis, and philosophical reflection, all delivered with a sense of intellectual urgency that has attracted a devoted following.

Zhao Jiaqi began uploading to Bilibili around 2018, when the platform's knowledge section was still in its formative stages. His early videos were not polished productions; they were the work of a hobbyist experimenting with the tools available to him. What distinguished them from the outset was their intellectual range. He did not confine himself to a single discipline. His videos moved fluidly between biology, history, technology, physics, sociology, and anthropology, unified not by subject matter but by a method of inquiry that he has described as "thinking while popularizing". He approached every topic with the same question: what does this tell us about how the world actually works, and what can we learn from it about our own condition? This commitment to synthesis, to finding connections across seemingly unrelated domains of knowledge, became his signature. By 2022, his channel had grown to over 500,000 followers, and he began to be recognized as one of the most promising voices in Bilibili's knowledge ecosystem. By January 2025, his follower count had reached 7.275 million, and he was named to Bilibili's Top 100 UP Creator list for both 2023 and 2024, with a third selection following in 2026 for the 2025 list.

The most important turning point in Siwei Shiyanshi's career was his decision to produce a comprehensive series on the history of the Chinese Communist Party. This was not a subject he approached casually. He spent years researching, citing sources, and building a narrative that treats the Party's early history not as a triumphalist fable but as a case study in organizational survival, strategic adaptation, and the economic and social forces that shaped the outcome of the Chinese revolution. The series, which he began releasing as paid membership content on Bilibili's charging platform, became a phenomenon. It is widely credited with transforming his financial sustainability; discussions among his viewers note that "it was the Party history series that made him this successful," and that his paid membership numbers are among the highest in Bilibili's knowledge category, with over 180,000 users paying monthly for access to his content. The series covers topics ranging from the founding of the Party and the establishment of its first armed forces to the decision to embark on the Long March and the strategic choices that determined the outcome of the civil war. What makes the series distinctive is its analytical method: he approaches these events through the lenses of economics, organizational theory, and internal political dynamics rather than relying on ideological framing alone. One widely recommended episode, "How Did 'Not Taking a Single Needle or Thread from the Masses' Lead to Encircling the Cities from the Countryside?", uses economic reasoning to explain how the Red Army's relationship with rural populations became a strategic asset.

Beyond the Party history series, Siwei Shiyanshi's video library encompasses an extraordinary range of subjects. His videos on the history of pandemics, including the Black Death and the 1918 influenza outbreak, combine epidemiological analysis with social history. His science videos explore topics as varied as the biology of bacteria, the physics of spectroscopy, and the mechanics of nuclear disasters. His video on the Chernobyl disaster has been widely cited for its clear explanation of the reactor design flaws and the human decisions that compounded them. A characteristic work, "Why Do People Let Themselves Be Deceived? Lessons from Pacific Islanders," examines the psychology of deception through an anthropological lens, using a specific historical case to illuminate a universal human vulnerability. Another recurring theme in his work is the relationship between technology and social change: he has produced videos on space colonization, artificial intelligence, and the history of medical innovation, always asking not only how these developments work but what they mean for human society. His content is characterized by a density of information that rewards attentive viewing. He does not pad his videos with filler; every minute is spent building an argument or introducing evidence. His delivery is fast-paced, a characteristic that some viewers find demanding but that his loyal audience regards as a sign of respect for their time and intelligence.

The social value of Siwei Shiyanshi's work lies in his demonstration that serious intellectual content can thrive on a platform better known for entertainment. He has built a career not by simplifying complex ideas into easily digestible fragments but by trusting his audience to follow sustained, rigorous analysis. His Party history series, in particular, has reached an audience far beyond the typical viewership for academic history, and it has been used by students, professionals, and general viewers as a resource for understanding a period that is often taught in simplified terms. His willingness to engage with difficult and politically sensitive subjects through a lens of evidence and reasoning rather than dogma has earned him respect across a wide spectrum of viewers. At the same time, his work has not been without criticism. Some observers have questioned the depth of his sourcing, and he has been the subject of online controversy regarding his political positioning and the rigor of his historical claims. He has addressed these criticisms in his own videos, acknowledging the limitations of his research while defending the value of his approach. His response to controversy, characterized by a willingness to engage rather than retreat, reflects the intellectual honesty that his most committed viewers value most.

In summary, Siwei Shiyanshi represents a model of the creator as a self-taught public intellectual. He has no formal training in the subjects he covers, yet he has built one of the most substantial and financially successful knowledge channels on Bilibili by applying a consistent method of inquiry to an extraordinary range of topics. His Party history series, in particular, has demonstrated that there is a large audience for analytical, source-based history presented without condescension or oversimplification. For Bilibili, he is evidence that the platform's knowledge section can support creators who take intellectual risks and expect their audiences to follow. For viewers, he offers a reminder that curiosity is not the exclusive province of the credentialed, and that the most valuable education is often the one you give yourself.
